newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firmer, interbank rate eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firmer, interbank rate eases late.

text.p: The Thai baht edged up against the dollar in late Wednesday trade in the onshore market buoyed by local exporter sales of the greenback, dealers said.
"The overall market was quiet. But there was some commercial selling of dollars by exporters," said one dealer at a major local bank.
The baht was quoted 29.01/29.06 to the dollar late in the onshore market compared with 29.10/29.20 in the morning.
Dealers said the baht had fallen to a level that exporters thought was right to take profit by selling dollars.
The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday announced the weighted average interbank exchange rate at 29.096 to the dollar against 28.922 on Tuesday.
In the offshore market, the baht was traded at 28.90/29.10 late against 28.830/28.930 in the morning.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was quoted at 20/25 satangs per dollar late in the domestic market and 25/45 in the offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 18-20 in late trade from 20 percent in the morning on rising liquidity, dealers said.
